constraints_honored: live writemybook DB never dropped or altered
all destructive ops scoped to wmb_restore_drill only
no destructive calls against other personas' data

row_counts_first_pass_slow_loop.note: 43s verification loop against a live, concurrently-written dev DB; documents/edit_findings appeared off by 1 due to concurrent writes during the loop, not a restore defect (see tight_window_reconciliation)

tight_window_reconciliation.method: captured before_dump and after_dump counts bracketing a second, fresh pg_dump (1.306s runtime), then compared final restore against both baselines
tight_window_reconciliation.conclusion: restored counts match after_dump exactly (documents 86=86=86, edit_findings 85=85), consistent with pg_dump's MVCC snapshot capturing committed state through its own transaction start on a live, concurrently-written source DB. No restore-fidelity defect; discrepancy fully explained by concurrent writes from other QA agents.

byte_identical_spot_check.scope: chapters x documents metadata (chapter_number, title, word_count, status, beta_score, beta_gate, type, current_version, storage_key), ordered by chapter_number
byte_identical_spot_check.caveat: manuscript prose itself lives in MinIO/S3 object storage, not Postgres; this spot check verifies DB-side metadata identity only, not prose-byte identity of object storage content

gaps_for_production: credentials must come from secrets manager, not .env
RTO must be re-measured against realistic prod-sized data (this dev drill: 32 tables, ~196KB dump, <15s total)
requires maintenance window or blue/green cutover strategy for a live prod restore
object storage (MinIO/S3) bucket backup/restore is a separate, unexercised leg required for a true DR guarantee
should be wrapped in an idempotent, logged, alerting automation script rather than run by hand
